stem: A nurse prepares medication from a multidose vial. Which practice best follows CDC safe-injection guidance?

options.A: Use a new sterile needle and syringe for every entry into the vial, and dedicate the multidose vial to one patient whenever possible.
options.B: Reuse the same needle for repeated vial entries if a new syringe is attached each time because the needle does not need replacement until visibly soiled.
options.C: Use one syringe for several patients if the needle is changed before each vial entry because needle replacement prevents contamination of the syringe.
options.D: Keep a shared multidose vial in the immediate patient-treatment area between doses because proximity improves access without increasing contamination risk.

rationale: CDC safe-injection guidance requires a new needle and new syringe when entering medication containers, recommends dedicating multidose vials to a single patient whenever possible, and states that multidose vials used for more than one patient should be kept in a clean medication-preparation area away from immediate patient-treatment areas. A follows these principles. B reuses a needle, C reuses a syringe across patients, and D places a shared vial in an area CDC specifically says to avoid.
educational_objective: Use a new sterile needle and syringe for every medication-vial entry and dedicate multidose vials to a single patient whenever possible to prevent injection-related transmission.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

source_original.stem: A nurse prepares medication from a multidose vial. Which practice best follows CDC safe-injection guidance?

options.A: Use a new sterile needle and syringe for every entry into the vial, and dedicate the multidose vial to one patient whenever possible in clinical practice.
options.B: Reuse the same needle for repeated vial entries if a new syringe is attached each time, because the needle does not need replacement until visibly soiled.
options.C: Use one syringe for several patients if the needle is changed before each vial entry, because needle replacement prevents contamination of the syringe.
options.D: Keep a shared multidose vial in the immediate patient-treatment area between doses, because proximity improves access without increasing contamination risk.

source_original.rationale: CDC safe-injection guidance requires sterile single-use injection equipment and recommends single-patient dedication of multidose vials whenever possible. Option A follows both principles. Option B reuses a needle, which is unsafe even if the syringe is changed. Option C reuses a syringe across patients, which CDC prohibits even if the needle is replaced. Option D places a shared multidose vial in the immediate treatment area, where CDC guidance says it should not be kept for multi-patient use.
source_original.source_detail: CDC Injection Safety — Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices: use a new sterile needle and syringe for every vial entry; dedicate multidose vials to a single patient whenever possible and keep shared vials away from immediate patient-treatment areas.
